old: I call for you on Agni, brightly shining, of fair praise, the guest of the clans, rich in good food, who like a friend has become one to be gained, a god among the god-devoted people, Jātavedas.
new: I call for you Agni, brightly shining, of fair praise, the guest of the clans, rich in good food, who like a friend has become one to be gained, a god among the god-devoted people, Jātavedas.
why: reviewer (minor): 'on Agni' is not in the Sanskrit (huve ... agnim, accusative object).

old: acc. pl. (pron.)

old: you

new: इसकी सेवा करते हुए भृगुओं ने उसे जलों के सहवास-स्थान में, जनों की बस्तियों में, दूसरी बार स्थापित किया। यह बहुलता सब पर छा जाए; देवों का परिचारक, तीव्र घोड़ों वाला अग्नि।
why: reviewer (minor): Hindi names Agni in the first half-verse, which has only imam (this one); English and notes keep it unnamed.

old: इसकी सेवा करते हुए भृगुओं ने उसे जलों के सहवास-स्थान में, जनों की बस्तियों में, दूसरी बार स्थापित किया। यह बहुलता सब पर छा जाए; देवों का परिचारक, तीव्र घोड़ों वाला अग्नि।

old: The gods placed Agni as one dear among the human clans, like a friend about to settle. May he shine through the eager nights, he who is worthy of vigour, in the house of the giver.
new: The gods placed Agni as one dear among the human clans, like those about to settle, a friend. May he shine through the eager nights, he who is worthy of vigour, in the house of the giver.
why: reviewer (error): kṣeṣyantaḥ is nom. pl. (the gram says so); it cannot qualify mitram (acc. sg.). The draft's 'friend about to settle' contradicts its own gram.

old: देवों ने मानव बस्तियों में अग्नि को प्रिय स्थापित किया, मानो बसने को उद्यत मित्र हो। वह उत्सुक रातों में चमके, जो बल के योग्य है, दानी के घर में।
new: देवों ने मानव बस्तियों में अग्नि को प्रिय स्थापित किया, बसने को उद्यत जनों की भाँति, मित्र को। वह उत्सुक रातों में चमके, जो बल के योग्य है, दानी के घर में।
why: reviewer (error): Same misattachment; also 'हो' adds a verb.

old: dhuḥ is a syncopated perfect (= dadhuḥ) of √dhā. ūrmyā 'night' and the sense of uśatīḥ 'eager' are uncertain; dakṣāyya is uncertain (taken as 'worthy of vigour'); the final ā after dame is left as a separate particle. The comparison 'like a friend about to settle' is the literal reading.
new: dhuḥ is a syncopated perfect (= dadhuḥ) of √dhā. ūrmyā 'night' and the sense of uśatīḥ 'eager' are uncertain; dakṣāyya is uncertain (taken as 'worthy of vigour'); the final ā after dame is left as a separate particle. The comparison 'like a friend about to settle' is the literal reading. Correction: kṣeṣyantaḥ is nominative plural and cannot agree with mitram (acc. sg.); the literal reading is 'like those about to settle, a friend'.
why: reviewer (minor): Notes call 'like a friend about to settle' the literal reading; it is not (nom. pl. participle).

old: His thriving is delightful, as of one's own; the appearance of him, the speeding, blazing one is the same. He who, bearing his tongue among the plants, shakes it about like a chariot horse its tail-hairs.
new: His thriving is delightful, as of one's own; the appearance of him, the speeding, blazing one. He who, bearing his tongue among the plants, shakes it about like a chariot horse its tail-hairs.
why: reviewer (error): 'is the same' is an unsupported added predicate; the clause is verbless.

old: His thriving is delightful, as of one's own; the appearance of him, the speeding, blazing one. He who, bearing his tongue among the plants, shakes it about like a chariot horse its tail-hairs.
new: His thriving is delightful, as of one's own; the appearance of him, the speeding, blazing one. He who, bearing his tongue among the plants, shakes the tail-hairs about like a steed, a chariot horse.
why: reviewer (error): Wrong object: jihvām is object of bharibhrat 'bearing'; vārān 'tail-hairs' is the object of dodhavīti. 'it' makes the tongue the thing shaken. Also atyaḥ 'steed' is dropped.

old: dakṣoḥ (read as genitive of dakṣu 'blazing') and hiyānasya 'speeding' are uncertain; saṃdṛṣṭi could also be 'sight' or 'vision'. The simile of the second line (jihvām as object of dodhavīti, vārān compared) is rendered literally; the exact syntax is unclear. In the translations the possessor 'his' is Agni, understood from the hymn; the verse itself does not name him.
new: dakṣoḥ (read as genitive of dakṣu 'blazing') and hiyānasya 'speeding' are uncertain; saṃdṛṣṭi could also be 'sight' or 'vision'. The simile of the second line (jihvām as object of dodhavīti, vārān compared) is rendered literally; the exact syntax is unclear. In the translations the possessor 'his' is Agni, understood from the hymn; the verse itself does not name him. Correction: jihvām is the object of bharibhrat; vārān is the object of dodhavīti, compared with atyaḥ ... rathyaḥ.
why: reviewer (minor): Notes repeat the wrong construction.

old: n. inst. sg.
new: n. nom./acc. sg. (adverbial or adjectival; -u stem, not inst.)
why: reviewer (error): An -u stem neuter cannot be instrumental (that would be raṃsunā); the form is nom./acc. n., adverbial or adjectival, so 'n. inst. sg.' is a wrong case label.
